scoringCalibration: One hair point is restored because the main root population now obeys an asymmetric hairline curve, the scalp density reaches true zero below it, and the visibly artificial legacy baby-hair mesh is removed. The score remains low because the extreme-top ribbon fan, repetitive side curtain, rear split and lack of production micro-transition fibers are still visible.
visualFindings: The forehead edge is now driven by the same asymmetric threshold in both scalp density and main-fiber root acceptance, so the previous broad geometric band is materially narrower.
The scalp density fades to zero below the authored hairline instead of leaving the old 10 percent dark floor over the upper forehead.
The sparse legacy HairlineBaby mesh and a rejected 168-strand comb-like replacement are absent; fixed front and three-quarter views no longer show detached forehead dashes.
The v55 tangent-preserving side flow and dedicated LOD1 remain intact while full export size falls to 7.88 MiB.
rejectedExperiments: v56 continuous mass-shell prototypes were rejected because a projected crown root created a smooth top ring and a boundary-extruded variant created dark side underlay without removing the top fan.
A 168-transition plus 58-baby-hair layout was rejected because synchronized strands formed an obvious comb across the forehead.
A reduced 26-baby-hair layout was rejected because the short fibers still read as a detached dotted line instead of integrated vellus hair.
blockingFailures: The extreme top view still exposes a radial fan of ribbon tips and fails the production silhouette gate.

The side lengths still read as a repetitive vertical curtain and need larger clump hierarchy, flyaways and ear-aware grouping.
The rear center still has a visible vertical separation and needs a more irregular overlapping root field.
Hair shading still needs an engine-side dual-lobe anisotropic model and strand-scale roughness variation.
The face still needs expression-oriented perioral loops, asymmetric commissure sculpting and a phoneme pose suite.
Integrated upper and lower eyelid thickness and expression-compatible canthus topology remain below review quality.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
